title: A Comprehensive Survey of Process Reward Models: Data Generation, Model Construction, and Usage
paper_type_zh: 过程奖励模型与过程监督综述
best_for_zh: 希望系统理解过程监督如何从数据走向训练与推理使用的读者。
one_line: A 2026 ACL survey that traces process reward models from labeled reasoning data through construction to search and reinforcement-learning use.
贯通过程数据生成、过程奖励模型构建与使用的 2026 年 ACL 综述。
why: It explains why a reasoning trace becomes process supervision only once intermediate states receive an explicit feedback contract.
inclusion_reason: A 2026 foundation that gives Track0 readers a unified route from reasoning traces to process labels, process reward models, test-time scaling, RL, and their distinct audit questions.

title: Problem
问题
html: Outcome reward models wait for a final answer. That is limiting when a system must tell whether an intermediate step is promising or choose among unfinished reasoning paths. Process reward models (PRMs) attach feedback to steps or trajectories instead. This survey follows that idea from process-data generation to model construction and use: prompts, intermediate states, feedback on those states, and applications such as search or reinforcement learning.
结果奖励模型要等到最终答案出现后才给分。当系统需要判断某一步是否有希望，或在多条未完成的推理路径中作选择时，这就不够了。过程奖励模型（PRM）改为在步骤或轨迹层级给出反馈。该综述沿着这一思路介绍过程数据生成、模型构建和实际使用：提示词、中间状态、附着其上的反馈，以及搜索和强化学习等用途。

title: Core idea
核心思路
html: The survey connects three questions: where process data comes from, how a PRM learns from it, and what later uses its scores. A reasoning trace is only written-out reasoning until its steps or full path receive labels, scores, or values. Those signals may come from people, judges, verifiers, or other models, so “process supervision” does not name one fixed kind of feedback. Finer local scores are useful only when they also help reach better final answers.
论文连接了三个问题：过程数据从哪里来，PRM 怎样从中学习，它的分数后来怎样被使用。推理轨迹起初只是写出来的推理过程；当步骤或整条轨迹被赋予标签、分数或价值时，才成为过程监督。反馈可以来自人类、裁判模型、验证器或其他模型，因此“过程监督”并不是一种固定的反馈。局部高分只有在能帮助得到更好最终答案时才真正有价值。

title: Method
方法
html: This is a map of the literature, not a release of one PRM. It covers process-data generation, PRM construction, test-time scaling, reinforcement learning, applications, and emerging benchmarks. The cited work varies in where traces come from, how finely they are labeled, who or what supplies feedback, and how scores shape search or training. Alongside the ACL page, PDF, checklist, DOI, and arXiv record, the authors provide a GitHub reading list organized around the same lifecycle; it is a curation resource, not a common PRM codebase or dataset.
这是一张文献地图，不是单个 PRM 的发布。它覆盖过程数据生成、PRM 构建、推理期扩展、强化学习、应用和新兴基准。被引研究的差异在于轨迹从哪里来、标签有多细、由谁或什么提供反馈，以及分数如何影响搜索或训练。除 ACL 页面、论文 PDF、清单、DOI 与 arXiv 外，作者还提供了按同一生命周期整理的 GitHub 阅读列表；它是文献导览资源，不是统一的 PRM 代码库或数据集。

title: Evidence
证据
html: The ACL Anthology record confirms the authors, ACL 2026 Long Papers venue, DOI, pages, checklist, and abstract. Its abstract supports the survey's coverage of the full pipeline and applications in mathematics, code, text, multimodal reasoning, robotics, and agents. It does not show that any one PRM works as a universal evaluator.
ACL Anthology 页面确认了作者、ACL 2026 长文会议信息、DOI、页码、清单和摘要。摘要说明该文覆盖完整流程，并讨论数学、代码、文本、多模态推理、机器人和智能体中的应用。这些材料说明的是综述覆盖了什么，并不表示某一个 PRM 已是普适可靠的评估器。

title: Novelty
新意
html: Process supervision and PRMs existed before this survey. Its contribution is to show them as one connected story: data generation, model construction, test-time scaling, reinforcement learning, and evaluation influence one another. This makes it easier to see why an improvement may come from richer labels, a stronger base model, more rollouts, a different verifier, or a different selection rule—not necessarily from the PRM alone.
过程监督与 PRM 早于这篇综述。它的贡献是把数据生成、模型构建、推理期扩展、强化学习和评测放进同一个故事里，让读者看到它们如何相互影响。这样也更容易理解：一次改进可能来自更丰富的标签、更强的基础模型、更多轨迹展开、不同的验证器或选择规则，而不一定完全来自 PRM。

title: Limitations
局限
html: The survey does not release a shared process dataset or define universal process labels. A label may reward fluent-looking reasoning rather than real progress, and comparisons across papers can blur differences in feedback source, search budget, or final-answer verification.
该综述不发布共享的过程数据集，也没有定义通用的过程标签。某些标签可能奖励看起来流畅的推理，而不是真实进展；不同论文的比较也可能掩盖反馈来源、搜索预算或最终答案验证方式的差异。

title: Usefulness
用途
html: The survey is a guide to the process-reward-model lifecycle: creating process data, building models, and using their scores. It separates raw reasoning traces, step-level labels, PRMs, search or selection mechanisms, and outcome rewards. It is useful for orientation rather than as a source of released labels, weights, or benchmarks.
这篇综述是理解过程奖励模型生命周期的向导：怎样生成过程数据，怎样构建模型，怎样使用它的分数。它区分原始推理轨迹、步骤标签、PRM、搜索或选择机制以及结果奖励。它适合帮助读者定位概念，而不是提供可直接使用的标签、模型权重或基准。

title: Reading notes
阅读笔记
html: Process reward models ask whether a reasoning step is moving in a useful direction, rather than waiting only for the final answer. They make feedback more detailed, but a good-looking step score does not automatically add up to a correct solution. Where the labels come from and how fine-grained they are changes what the score means.
过程奖励模型把“这一步推理是否朝着有用方向前进”变成可以学习的信号，而不只等待最终答案揭晓。它让反馈更细，但看起来好的步骤分数不一定会累积成正确解答。标签来自哪里、划分得多细，都会改变这个分数的含义。
